name: Algerian
description: Algerian (or Algerian Patience) is a grand, two-deck solitaire game noted for its complex layout and unique 'dual-direction' foundations. Unlike most solitaires that build in one direction, Algerian requires players to manage four foundations ascending from Ace and four descending from King simultaneously. With a wrapping tableau and a multi-stage redeal mechanic, it is a game of deep tactical planning and endurance.

content.text: Algerian (or Algerian Patience) is a grand, two-deck solitaire game noted for its complex layout and unique 'dual-direction' foundations. Unlike most solitaires that build in one direction, Algerian requires players to manage four foundations ascending from Ace and four descending from King simultaneously. With a wrapping tableau and a multi-stage redeal mechanic, it is a game of deep tactical planning and endurance.

First documented by the author 'Tarbart' in the 1905 publication 'Games of Patience'. Its name suggests an exotic origin, though it is more likely an English invention from the Victorian/Edwardian era fascination with North African themes.
One player only. Algerian is a solitaire (patience) game played by a single player.
Two standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards).

1. **Foundations**: 8 slots (initially empty or 4 Aces/4 Kings placed if drawn). 2. **Tableau**: 8 depots with 1 card each. 3. **Reserve**: 6 piles with 4 cards each. 4. **Stock**: Remainder of the 104 cards.

items.text: Carthage: Similar to Algerian but with slightly different stock-dealing rules and no wrapping on the tableau.
